key_insight: A complete symmetry-invariant descriptor basis connects magnetic textures to response tensors through interpretable order parameters that remain uncorrelated as higher spin orders are added.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports interpretable prediction of magnetic-crystal responses, including anomalous Hall conductivity, for materials modeling and screening.
method: Construct symmetry-invariant descriptors for arbitrary crystal structures and magnetic textures.
Modify principal component analysis to obtain hierarchically stable, uncorrelated order parameters.
Use these features for regression and classification of anomalous Hall conductivity in a magnetic kagome lattice.
evidence_signal: In the regime where linear regression models anomalous Hall conductivity well, ranked squared regression coefficients follow a Zipf-like power law; the abstract reports no numerical accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Although the descriptor construction is general, the abstract demonstrates prediction only for a magnetic kagome lattice, leaving transferability and higher-order computational cost unquantified.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Response Tensors in Crystalline Magnets: Application to Kagome Metals
